title: Romantic Valentine proposal page with evasive No button and Yes celebration meme

requirements.text: Create a single-page romantic Valentine prompt UI that asks: "Will you be my Valentine?" with exactly two prominent options: "Yes" and "No", using a pink-and-white romantic theme.

quotes: Create an interactive web page as a surprise for my girlfriend... ask her to be my Valentine. There should be two options: Yes or No.
The page should be themed romantically with a pink and white color scheme

acceptanceCriteria: Landing view shows one clear question: "Will you be my Valentine?"
Exactly two visible choices are present: a "Yes" button and a "No" button
Overall styling uses a coherent pink-and-white romantic theme (background, typography, button styles)
The page works in Chrome on iPad-sized screens without layout overflow or clipped controls

requirements.text: Implement interactive behavior for the "No" button so that when the user attempts to interact with it (mouse hover on desktop; touch/pointer interaction on iPad), it moves to a new position within the viewport/container, preventing the user from clicking it.

quotes: When she hovers her cursor over No, it should move away so she cannot click it, forcing her to click only on Yes.
...easily run it on my iPad using Chrome.

acceptanceCriteria: On desktop: moving the cursor over the "No" button causes it to reposition before a click can occur
On touch devices (e.g., iPad Chrome): attempting to tap/press the "No" button causes it to reposition, making it effectively unclickable
The "No" button remains visible on-screen after moving (does not move off-canvas)
The "Yes" button remains stable and clickable throughout

requirements.text: When the user clicks "Yes", transition the UI to a celebratory state that displays a meme image and the text: "Good choice".

quotes: When she clicks Yes, show her a meme image telling her "Good choice

acceptanceCriteria: Clicking "Yes" reliably switches the view/state to a celebration screen (or modal)
The celebration view displays the exact text: "Good choice"
The celebration view displays the provided/generated meme image (served as a static frontend asset)
The initial question and buttons are no longer the primary focus once "Yes" is clicked (hidden or clearly de-emphasized)

requirements.text: Add the required static image asset(s) to the frontend and render them directly from the frontend (no backend routing), ensuring they load correctly in production builds.
acceptanceCriteria: All generated images are placed under frontend/public/assets/generated
The "Yes" success state renders the meme image from frontend/public/assets/generated via a static path
No backend changes are required for serving images

constraints: Do not edit files under frontend/src/components/ui or any other immutable paths listed in SYSTEM_CONTEXT.
Keep the app as a single-page experience focused only on asking to be Valentine and the resulting success state.
No backend canister features are required for this request.
nonGoals: Additional pages, navigation, or multi-step flows
Integrations with external APIs or third-party services

required: Meme-style romantic image with the words "Good choice" (valentine-good-choice-meme.dim_1024x1024.png)
